scope: Repository-level auth/session/redirect/password-recovery security review. R06 remains RED until M01/M03 are fully accepted and deployed recovery/session behavior is proven.

controls.expected: Browser config contains only Supabase publishable key and no service-role material
Access/refresh tokens remain memory-only; no localStorage/sessionStorage persistence
Reset success text does not disclose whether an account exists
Reset redirect is constructed from location.origin plus fixed /demo/auth-recovery.html and URL-encoded
Auth and recovery pages set no-referrer policy
Only type=recovery with an access token is accepted
expires_at is checked when supplied and expired recovery sessions fail closed
Recovery URL fragment is removed immediately after parsing while token remains memory-only
Password update uses PATCH /auth/v1/user with bearer recovery access token
In-memory access token is cleared after successful password update

external_runtime_evidence_required: The deployed recovery URL must be present in Supabase Auth allowed redirect URLs.
A real reset email must redirect to the deployed recovery page with a valid recovery session.
A real password update must complete successfully and the consumed session must not remain reusable.
M01 and M03 must be fully accepted before R06 can become GREEN.
documentation_basis: Supabase Auth documentation: resetPasswordForEmail redirectTo/RedirectTo must target an allowlisted redirect URL.
Supabase Auth documentation: recovery sessions may be delivered in URL fragments; client-side recovery handling is required for fragment sessions.
